finding.claim: OS command injection in GET /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a string passed to exec(), which runs it through /bin/sh -c, so shell metacharacters in host execute arbitrary commands. Output is returned to the client, so the attack is not blind.

trace.note: Route handler receives query string; no auth middleware
req.query.host concatenated into command string passed to exec (shell)
Combined stdout returned to client via res.send(out), making injected output readable

finding.guards_checked: No validation or allowlist on host (no net.isIP or hostname regex); no shell escaping; exec used instead of execFile/spawn with argv array; no shell:false; no authentication or authorization on route. Express array/object query values still concatenate to a string, so they do not block injection. PoC by reading only, not executed: GET /ping?host=127.0.0.1;id -> shell runs 'ping -c 1 127.0.0.1;id'; last command exit 0 so err is null and out contains both outputs. Suggested fix: execFile('ping', ['-c','1','--',host], cb) plus strict IP/hostname validation.

verdict.guard_found: none. tools.js:6 is an unauthenticated route with no auth middleware. tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into a string passed to exec(), which runs through /bin/sh, with no validation, escaping, or argv-array form. The only check, `if (err)` at tools.js:8, runs after the command and does not filter input. tools.js:11 returns stdout to the client, so injected output is visible.
verdict.reason: The route at tools.js:6 needs no credentials, and tools.js:7 passes the unsanitized req.query.host into exec(), which the shell interprets, so metacharacters such as `;id` run arbitrary commands and tools.js:11 returns their output. All trace lines match the candidate's description.

finding.claim: No authentication on any route and server binds to all interfaces via app.listen(3001) with no host argument, exposing /ping command execution (F1) plus host info via /uptime and /version to any network peer.
finding.source: Any network peer that can reach TCP port 3001 (default bind is all interfaces)
finding.sink: app.listen(3001) (tools.js:28) exposing handlers at tools.js:6, 15, 24 including exec in /ping and host info in /uptime (tools.js:25) and /version (tools.js:16)

trace.note: Listens on all interfaces; no host argument
/ping handler has no auth check (enables F1 remotely)
/version returns git HEAD hash without auth

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware; no per-route authorization; no host binding restriction; no reverse proxy or firewall config in repo (repo contains only tools.js). Adding auth is an authorization change requiring review. Suggested fix: bind to 127.0.0.1 or add authentication before exposing routes.

verdict.guard_found: none. No auth middleware or per-route checks exist in tools.js (lines 6, 15, 24 are bare handlers). app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 has no host argument, so it is not restricted to loopback. The repo contains only tools.js, so no firewall or reverse-proxy control is visible here.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the file: tools.js:28 listens without a host argument, and the unauthenticated handlers at tools.js:6 (/ping), :16 (/version), and :25 (/uptime) have no guard, so any network peer that can reach port 3001 can call them. The claim overstates one point: /version (tools.js:16) returns the git HEAD hash, which is repository information rather than host information.
